key_insight: Frustrated Gd3+ double perovskites, Ba2GdSbO6 and Sr2GdSbO6, enable exceptionally low-temperature adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration, reaching sub-100 mK performance with record-low ADR temperatures for Gd3+ magnets under the stated conditions.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer a promising solid-state route to ultra-low-temperature cooling for quantum technologies, especially where compact, high-entropy-density refrigerants are needed.
method: Synthesize and characterize Ba2GdSbO6 and Sr2GdSbO6 double perovskites with Gd3+ magnetic ions.
Measure magnetocaloric/ADR behavior starting from 2 K under applied magnetic fields up to 5 T.
Compare cooling performance, entropy density, and ordering temperatures under finite-field and zero-field conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports cooling to 67–68 mK in finite fields and 78–83 mK in zero field, with entropy densities of 189 and 201 mJ K-1 cm-3.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on small samples under controlled laboratory conditions, so scaling, thermal coupling, and magnetic-field hardware constraints will matter in practical ADR systems.
paper_title: Frustrated Gd3+ Double Perovskites as High-Performance Magnetocaloric Materials for Sub-100 mK Adiabatic Demagnetization Refrigeration
